title: Tool kits return incomplete
whatItTeaches: Map possible causes under categories, connect each branch to the outcome, and choose which links deserve evidence.
problemStatement: A fictional lending library found missing parts in five of its last thirty returned tool kits. Which causes should the volunteers investigate first?

seats.persona: A volunteer focused on observable evidence.

submissions.categories-input: Packing process covers checks before a kit leaves. Kit design covers how parts are held and labeled inside the case; these differ even when the same volunteer sees both.
submissions.causes-input: Packing process > no pre-loan count > blank count box on four affected loan cards. Blank boxes are observed; kits leaving incomplete is still an inference.
submissions.checks-input: Count every part before and after ten loans and photograph the packed tray. If parts are already missing before departure, packing explains some cases; if counts drop later, investigate return and storage.

seats.persona: A volunteer focused on alternatives and practical constraints.

submissions.categories-input: Return handoff covers the exchange at the desk. Borrower instructions covers what people are told to count or report before returning a kit.
submissions.causes-input: Kit design > small bit slips behind foam > loose foam in two affected cases. Return handoff > rushed check > no return checklist. The physical gaps are observed; parts escaping is untested.
submissions.checks-input: Before those loans, inspect behind the foam without changing it and record the result. Finding the supposedly missing bits in a case would favor the kit-design branch over borrower loss.

scores.evidence: Investigate packing first: blank pre-loan count boxes could allow an incomplete kit to leave, but blank records do not prove that happened. Keep kit design as a competing category: loose foam could conceal small bits rather than a borrower losing them. Inspect behind the foam and record before-and-after part counts plus tray photos for ten loans. Parts missing before departure favor packing; parts found behind foam favor kit design.
